classes.subject: PLSCI
classes.titleLong: Field Lab in Global Plant Biodiversity and Vegetation

notes.descrlong: Taught in Patagonia. Class travels to Patagonia (Chile) on January 2 and returns on January 19, 2025. Students must enroll in PLSCI 2302 during the spring semester to receive a final grade.

classes.description: An intensive three-week field course in Latin America over winter break (most years taken in Patagonia) studying local vegetation and flora and the relationship of vegetation to climate, geography and geology. In the field, students will receive lectures on the vegetation, learn to identify dominant plants, and undertake a directed set of vegetation transects that record species diversity and ecological parameters.
classes.catalogComments: Students must enroll in PLSCI 2301 to receive a final grade in PLSCI 2302.
catalogOutcomes: Interpret the distribution of vegetation in relation to climate and soils.
Observe carefully in the field, take precise and easily interpretable field notes, conduct collaborative scientific data collection and analysis.
Identify plant species in the field.
Exercise specific methods of data collection using ecological transects.

classes.subject: PLSCI

notes.descrlong: This Winter Session class is offered by the School of Continuing Education and Summer Sessions. For details visit: https://sce.cornell.edu/courses/roster.

classes.description: Focuses on helping individuals understand how scientific information relates to the issues they face as citizens, in management decision making, and in public policy. To what extent should genetic engineering of crop plants be permitted? Should we place limits on fossil fuel consumption as a means of limiting global warming and global climate change? Must human endeavors be restricted in certain areas to maintain diversity? The format of this course is interactive, with lectures and discussions about how we as a society deal with controversial issues. This course is suitable for life sciences majors.
catalogOutcomes: Explain, evaluate, and effectively interpret basic concepts in cell and molecular biology.
Explain, evaluate, and effectively interpret basic concepts in general ecology and biodiversity.
Integrate qualitative information to reach defensible and creative conclusions about the impacts of climate change, genetic engineering, and biodiversity on the natural world and society.
Communicate effectively through writing, speech, and visual information via written exams, writing assignments and class discussion concerning the above topics.
Articulate the views of people with diverse perspectives on the above issues.

classes.subject: PLSCI
classes.titleLong: Far Beyond Ithaca (FBI): Plant Explorations in Winter

notes.descrlong: Prerequisite: PLSCI 3400, plus CLASS 2640 or PLSCI 2100 or PLSCI 3100. Enrollment preference given to: Classics, Agricultural Sciences, and Plant Sciences majors. This is part two of a multi-semester course, running January 6, 2025 - January 15, 2025 in the Peruvian Amazon. To apply, please contact Leah Cook (lcc2).

classes.description: In sections of this course, students travel with faculty to a domestic or international locale to experience first-hand the issues around a particular challenge in plant sciences, such as climate change and the spread of plant diseases, drought and viticulture, and the tension between biodiversity, species conservation and large-scale agriculture. Students engage with communities, collect and analyze data, and collaborate with peers in a final presentation at the end of the course.
classes.catalogComments: Students must enroll in PLSCI 3400 to receive a final grade in PLSCI 3401.
classes.catalogFee: Fees for associated winter trip will vary by class section.
classes.catalogPermission: Enrollment preference given to: Plant Sciences and Agricultural Sciences majors.
catalogOutcomes: Describe the state of plant communities and/or agroecosystems in the targeted region.
Determine how humans are interfacing with these systems to create challenges or to help mitigate problems.
Explain how events in the targeted region can have impacts at home.
